text:
Ruben (vendor ops): Hi team — DataStream SpA (CL) emailed asking Redwood to gross-up their invoice to cover 15% Chilean withholding. They say local law requires withholding on cross-border service payments. They attached a "Certificado de Residencia Fiscal" and RUT 76.123.456-7.
Eleni (finance): Do we have a gross-up clause in the contract/SOW? Usually gross-ups are only done if contractually required. If not, we pay the invoice as billed and the vendor handles withholding with local tax authorities.
Nolan (acct exec): Contract doesn't mention gross-up. SLA/PRicing schedules are net amounts. Vendor insists they won't accept net because of mandatory WHT.
Sofia (tax): Quick notes: Chile applies withholding on certain payments to non-residents, but for residents (local entities) the mechanics differ. If DataStream is a Chilean resident (RUT present), they won't need treaty relief — they're domestic. Why are they asking Redwood (US entity) to gross-up? Usually gross-up is for payments to non-residents where payer must withhold.
Ruben (vendor ops): Their AP says the payer (Redwood) must withhold 15% when paying a foreign client, but they're local. Confusing. They claim our payments are routed via a Netherlands entity and therefore treated as outbound to a non-resident. They want gross-up to get the agreed net.
TaxBot: High-level: withholding rules depend on payer/resident status and payment route. If payment originates from an offshore affiliate, local WHT may apply. Need evidence of payer entity used for payment and country of remittance.
Eleni (finance): Action: Ask for copy of the payment instruction that shows payment originating entity + beneficiary bank details. Also request the Certificado de Residencia Fiscal (signed by SII) if they claim Chilean residency, and any official tax notice requiring payer gross-up.
Mila (payments): Operationally, we do not gross-up unless legal approves. If we pay gross, we need Treasury sign-off. I will flag the AP hold: "DO NOT GROSS-UP" until tax confirms.
Ruben (vendor ops): I asked them for payment routing and their SII certificate. They replied with a PDF (cert_residencia.pdf) and an email saying payments from Redwood NL branch will be processed this quarter.
Sofia (tax): If payment is routed from NL and treated as payment to a non-resident, Chilean law may require withholding at source. But gross-up is a commercial negotiation point — payer not typically forced to gross-up unless contract. We can offer to pay the gross amount if they reissue an invoice showing grossed-up total and include explicit tax calculation. That shifts the administrative burden to vendor.
Nolan (acct exec): Customer is pushing for prompt payment. Can we offer two paths: 1) Redwood pays invoice amount as-is and vendor handles any withholding with SII, or 2) vendor reissues invoice with gross-up included (we'll pay total) and attach SII/residency docs and bank routing.
Ruben (vendor ops): Vendor prefers Redwood to gross-up on our side. They say they can't reissue because their systems don't support gross-up lines.
Eleni (finance): Noted. Sofia, do we need a written tax opinion to be comfortable grossing-up?
Sofia (tax): Yes — I need confirmation of applicable withholding rate and legal basis. Also want evidence that Redwood's NL payment will be caught by Chilean WHT. If it's ambiguous, we can ask vendor to request a certificate of tax residency and/or a binding interpretation from SII. For now, policy: DO NOT GROSS-UP without legal sign-off.
Mila (payments): Flagged in billing: "HOLD: WHT/GROSS-UP dispute. DO NOT PAY UNTIL RESOLVED."
Ruben (vendor ops): Update from vendor: they forwarded a scanned payroll-like memo from their tax advisor saying 15% WHT will apply if payer is non-resident. They are pushing for immediate payment.
Nolan (acct exec): Offer made: we can do a provisional payment net of 15% and issue a covering note promising to review once final docs come in. That might upset vendor.
Eleni (finance): Instead: offer to expedite payment if they reissue invoice either (a) grossed-up, or (b) with a tax withholding line showing the withheld amount. If they can't reissue, we pay net & include a statement that vendor must seek credit/refund locally.
Sofia (tax): I'll review the Certificado de Residencia and the advisor memo. If it shows they're Chilean resident and payment actually originates from Redwood CL or Redwood US subsidiary, withholding might not apply. If payment originates from NL, we may need WHT. I'll update by EOD.
TaxBot: Reminder: keep PDFs/evidence in tax_evidence/2024/cl_74-1234567 for audit trail.
Mila (payments): Documentation note added. Payment hold remains.
Sofia (tax): Quick follow-up: Certificate looks like an SII stamped residency certificate — that's strong. However, it shows company legal name "DATASTREAM SPA" and RUT 76.123.456-7. It doesn't prove payment routing. Ask finance to confirm paying entity (Redwood Inference US vs NL).
Eleni (finance): Payment will originate from Redwood NL for that contract (we used EU billing entity). I'll log that in the thread.
Sofia (tax): If paying entity is NL, Chilean WHT may apply. Without a contractual gross-up we shouldn't unilaterally gross-up. Proposed path: 1) Vendor issues grossed-up invoice OR 2) Redwood pays net and withholds per Chile rules and provides vendor a withholding certificate (retention document) so they can credit it with SII.
Ruben (vendor ops): I'll relay options. Vendor prefers us to pay gross.
Nolan (acct exec): If vendor insists, we can negotiate a one-time amendment to the PO to include gross-up and get legal sign-off. But not a default policy.
Mila (payments): Closing: holding payment until vendor chooses option or until tax/legal sign-off. I set billing flag and ticket in AR. :lock:
Sofia (tax): I'll draft a short note to vendor explaining options and next steps. If they send a reissued gross-up invoice we'll need a signed statement accepting the new amount.
Ruben (vendor ops): Will send vendor the options now. Will update thread when they reply. :spiral_calendar:
